summary: Iteration 58 — Record-level access control (Case 1) + Duplicate/My Leads filters (Case 2). Backend: 16/16 pytest cases pass covering caller-sees-all, ensure_lead_edit denial on 8 mutation endpoints + click-to-dial, assign→edit-allowed→revert flow, admin unrestricted edits, duplicate=true filter (total=1 regardless of active). Frontend: caller readonly-banner + access-denied-modal verified for 9/10 gated actions on foreign lead #133223; filter-duplicate dropdown and my-leads-toggle work for caller; admin sees filter-duplicate (SELECT) with 'Duplicate Leads only' shrinking list to 1 and chip 'Duplicate Lead: Only' appearing; my-leads-toggle correctly hidden for admin. ONE frontend defect: caller-activity-add does NOT trigger access-denied-modal because <CallerActivities/> at LeadDetail.jsx:352 is instantiated without canEdit / onDenied props.

ui_bugs.issue: Missing canEdit={canEdit} and onDenied={deny} props. As a result, on a read-only lead the caller can type feedback and click 'Add More Note' → POST returns 403 which surfaces as a toast instead of the required access-denied-modal. The other gated child components (FieldCard/QACard/CustomFieldsCard/FollowUpSection) receive these props correctly.

action_items: Pass canEdit + onDenied props to <CallerActivities/> instance in LeadDetail.jsx (line 352), matching the pattern used for FieldCard/QACard/CustomFieldsCard/FollowUpSection. This is the only remaining gap for full record-level UI enforcement.

rca of the issue: CallerActivities component accepts canEdit + onDenied props (defaults canEdit=true, onDenied=noop) and gates its add() with 'if (!canEdit) return onDenied()'. But at LeadDetail.jsx:352 it is rendered as <CallerActivities leadId={lead.id} onCount={...} /> with no canEdit/onDenied — so the default true is used and the modal is never triggered. The 403 backend response then surfaces as a generic toast (via apiErr(e)). Fix: pass canEdit={canEdit} onDenied={deny}.
